name: Gernika Peace Museum (Museo de la Paz)
story: On the afternoon of Monday 26 April 1937 – market day – aircraft of the German Condor Legion, with Italian Aviazione Legionaria bombers, attacked Gernika for about three hours in support of the Nationalist advance on Bilbao. Explosive and incendiary bombs destroyed most of the town centre, while the Rentería bridge and the arms factories on the edge of town survived. The raid, reported worldwide by journalists including George Steer and painted by Picasso, became the defining image of the bombing of civilians. The Peace Museum, on the main square, tells the story of the raid through survivors' testimony and places it in a wider history of war and reconciliation, including Germany's 1997 apology.
see: A modern museum with a reconstructed 1937 house interior, survivor testimony, audiovisuals and a section on peace and reconciliation.
plan: Foru Plaza 1, opposite the town hall. Closed on Mondays from mid-October to mid-March; entry €6.50 (reduced €4.50); English group tours can be booked in advance.

boxes.text: Death toll: the Basque Government reported 1,645 dead in 1937; most modern historians put it between about 126 and 300; Xabier Irujo (2017) argues for a much higher figure. Records were destroyed and both sides used the numbers for propaganda.
